summary: A 1943 state steel fire tower moved from Pine Mountain was replaced by an AT&T tower in 1945, which the register lists as built 1945; a 2024 blog says it still stands in some form.

facts.design: Steel tower; top cab now holds AT&T communication equipment; old fire cab moved to a lower level
facts.status_note: A 2024 blog post says it still exists in some form. Condition and staffing were not confirmed.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

events.note: State steel fire tower built in 1943 and moved here from Pine Mountain. The move date is not given.
The state fire tower was removed in 1945
AT&T built a replacement tower on the same location for its communication equipment. The register lists 1945 as the build year.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, September 16, 2008
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 3, 2014
A 2024 blog post describes a visit and says the tower still exists in some form

corrections.proposed: 1943 state steel fire tower built and moved from Pine Mountain; removed 1945. AT&T replacement tower built 1945 on the same location.
corrections.why: The register's Built 1945 date refers to the AT&T replacement tower. The state fire tower it replaced dates from 1943, according to the Former Fire Lookout Sites entry.

sources.title: Ascending to Pennsylvania's Clarks Knob Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: Current status rests on one 2024 blog post. No access rules, climbing guidance, staffing status, or notable fires were found. The Eastern US Lookouts page for this site has no readable content, so it is not cited. Facebook posts repeat the register wording but could not be opened, so they are not cited.
